scope: Independent code/FFI review, finite baseline-vs-candidate preflight differential, real LLVM machine/link tests. Not full-language, whole-workspace, performance or product acceptance.

findings: Official LLVM23.1.4 Core.h declares LLVMContextSetDiscardValueNames(LLVMContextRef, LLVMBool); Types.h defines LLVMBool as int, matching Rust c_int.
Value.cpp::setNameImpl exempts GlobalValue from discard. Existing builder global/function/type creation names remain intact; only local SSA/parameter/basic-block labels are omitted.
Configuration is applied after complete structured preflight and before module/Builder creation in a per-request, non-null, owned context. Text-reference path keeps its previous configuration.
Model name validation, name-to-handle maps and readable machine sidecar are unchanged. Object alpha-renaming and real exported symbol/external call tests pass.
Fast return is after every type/name/CFG/phi/predecessor/dominance check.

For each non-phi use, any non-phi definition in a later textual block disables the shortcut. Same-block forward references still reject, earlier blocks/parameters are already available, and all phi handles are precreated.
Returning the enumerated non-phi positions preserves each block's instruction/effect order. Cross-block construction order has no runtime side effect.
Original Kahn dependency edges, deduplication and cycle diagnostic remain as fallback for forward references, including unreachable non-phi cycles.
Independent differential and schedule-validity audit found no mismatch in 1493 cases; finite coverage is not a general formal proof.
